newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Indonesia's Suharto in Cambodia for three-day trip.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Suharto in Cambodia for three-day trip.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto arrived in Cambodia on Monday, his first stop on a visit to three countries seeking to join the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).
Cambodian officials and analysts said Suharto's visit would help strengthen political and trade ties and was expected to raise hopes Phnom Penh would join ASEAN later this year.

Suharto, who last visited Cambodia in 1968, was met at the airport by King Norodom Sihanouk, co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen as well as colourfully-dressed ethnic minorities and children.
Thousands of children waved flags as Suharto's delegation of more than 50 government and business officials, including Foreign Minister Ali Alatas, were driven to the royal palace.

He met formally with King Sihanouk, his host for the next three days, and was scheduled to hold formal talks on bilateral, regional and international issues with the co-premiers and top government officials on Tuesday morning.
Cambodia, Burma and Laos are set to join the seven-nation ASEAN together, possibly later this year when the organisation celebrates its 30th anniversary.
Current members are Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, Singapore and Vietnam.

"This visit paves the road for Cambodia's entry into ASEAN...It shows ASEAN is committed to promoting the peace process in this country and ASEAN is supportive of Cambodia's entry," said one political analyst.
Commerce Minister Cham Prasidh also said the visit augured well for Cambodia's chances of joining ASEAN this year.
The analyst said Jakarta was playing down the role of ASEAN in Suharto's trip to avoid upstaging Malaysia, which will lead the grouping when Cambodia could be admitted later this year.

"It will help, I'm sure it will help. It's not designed for this...(but) it will help," Indonesian Ambassador Hamid Alhadad said, when asked if the visit would boost chances of Cambodia getting into the regional bloc this year.
Officials in Jakarta have said Suharto's visit to Cambodia, Laos and Burma was not designed to focus on ASEAN.
The two countries were scheduled to sign agreements underpinning ties, including a trade pact and a memorandum of understanding on oil and gas exploration and production, officials said.
"We have to develop more trade between our two countries," Cham Prasidh told Reuters on Monday, adding that two-way trade totalled only around $10-15 million each year.
Finance Secretary of State Chanthol Sun, who said the visit "shows a confidence in the country", hoped it would bring more business, adding that there was not much Indonesian investment.
Indonesia gives modest amounts of aid to Cambodia and has provided military assistance to the royal armed forces, including training special forces troops.
